newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court annuls Commission's state aid framework for cars.
newsitem.headline: Court annuls Commission's state aid framework for cars.

text.p: The European Court of Justice annuled on Tuesday a European Commission decision to extend its framework for state aid in the car industry.
The court said the Commission extended its mandatory notification policies for state aid to car manufacturers without proper consultation with member states.

The Commission justified its decision to prolong existing rules already agreed by member states by an overriding Community interest to protect against undistorted competition in the motor vehicle industry.

The court accepted Spain's arguments that any decision to extend rules beyond thier expiry date requires the same member state consultation and agreement as if the rules were being adopted for the first time.

"The framework ceases to exist on the date which it is set to expire...and a decision to prolong it...after the date of expiry...constitutes a modification...and must be adopted according to the same procedure...as the original framework or of a decision making modifications to it," the court said.
Kingdom of Spain v European Commission

application for annulment of the Commission's decision, notified by letter of 6 July 1995 (OJ 1995 C 284, p. 3) to prolong, with retroactive effect from 1 January 1995, its decision of 23 December 1992 which had itself prolonged the validity of the Community framework on state aid to the motor vehicle industry

1. Annuls the Commission's decision, notified by letter of 6 July 1995 (OJ 1995 C 284, p. 3) to prolong, with retroactive effect from 1 January 1995, its decision of 23 December 1992 which had itself prolonged the validity of the Community framework on state aid to the motor vehicle industry
2. Orders the Commission to pay the costs.
